answer.rationale: With the primary contract lapsing in 14 days and no auto-renew, and the line already running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, delivery continuity is the dominant risk this cycle. The incumbent has already refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms is not viable this cycle, and switching primary vendor now would introduce onboarding and invoicing-transition risk exactly when there is no slack to absorb any disruption (contrasting with memory_c2's report of smooth onboarding, which was under different, less time-pressured conditions). Adding a second source doesn't resolve the expiring primary contract itself, and deferring is unsafe given no auto-renew clause. Renewing the incumbent (supported by memory_c1's record of stable, uninterrupted continuity across prior cycles) protects delivery risk immediately, though it does not satisfy the 18% cost mandate this cycle — that gap is flagged as a downstream value risk to be addressed via renegotiation or second-sourcing in the next review cycle once time pressure eases. I verified memory_c1 and memory_c2 to directly compare the stability claim against the cost-cutting switch claim before committing.
